verdicts.title: Write BoundBits delegated mutators through the width-validating store
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically on a patched copy (all claims held: setall/invert/sort write through; fill() raises ValueError 'Expected 4 bits, got 8' with the struct untouched; readers/return values pass through unchanged incl. int from index(), searchiterator, copy(); exceptions mid-call leave the struct untouched because write-back only runs after a successful return; masked-backend (bitvector_speedup) behavior byte-identical to pristine incl. unchanged AttributeError for setall; the wrapper's only backend requirements, copy() and __eq__, exist on all three implementations; new tests skip cleanly on the non-bitarray backend; full suite 856 passed matching the claim). Nits, no action strictly required: (1) unmentioned behavior delta -- pickle.dumps(bb.to01) succeeded on pristine (bound method of a throwaway derivation) but now raises (the 'delegated' local closure is unpicklable); exotic and arguably meaningless before, but the risks section's saved-method paragraph should mention it. (2) bitarray's bytereverse on a sub-byte field now writes through bitarray's padded-byte semantics (4-bit 0b0001 -> 0b0000 because the 4 hidden pad bits participate in the per-byte reversal) -- faithful delegation and width-preserving, but it converts a silent no-op into a surprising-but-persisted result; worth one comment line since the new __getattr__ comment names bytereverse as an example mutator. (3) Measured overhead on delegated readers: bb.count(1) 8.1 -> 13.9 us/call, bb.to01() 6.7 -> 13.2 us/call (~2x); consistent with the acknowledged cost, fine for a non-hot path.

verdicts.title: Detach-copy Struct-valued field defaults per instance at __init__ bind time
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically on the patched copy: scalar field() default, plain 'a: Inner = Inner(3)' spelling, and array-element defaults all detach per instance (identity False, cross-instance mutation isolated); explicit-arg aliasing preserved for a genuinely separate shared instance; nested Struct-in-Struct default detaches deeply (t1.mid.inner is not t2.mid.inner); generator array default of Structs materializes then detaches correctly; ill-typed/mixed/wrong-length defaults raise the identical error type+message as pristine; parse() unaffected; pack roundtrip and copy type fidelity confirmed; _bm_e loop-var collision impossible (metaclass rejects _bm_-prefixed field names with PlanCompileError, verified); full suite 856 passed with the pinned test replaced 1-for-1 as the only test change (baseline 854). The maintainer-decision flag is honest (names the reversed pinned test, presents default_factory as the no-silent-copy alternative). One real corner the fix text papers over: the trigger is OBJECT IDENTITY with the default, not 'parameter left at its default' -- explicitly passing the exact default object (e.g. a module-level DEFAULT=Inner(5) used as field(default=DEFAULT) and later Outer(a=DEFAULT)) gets detach-copied, violating the documented 'explicit assignment keeps live reference semantics' in exactly that case (verified: pristine aliases, patched copies). A _MISSING-sentinel parameter default would close the corner at the cost of uglier introspected __init__ defaults; at minimum the fix/docstring wording should say 'identical to the default object' rather than 'left at its default'. Sole-user weighting makes this a nit, not a blocker.

verdicts.title: Make the Codec protocol docstring state the real membership and pack convention
verdicts.issues: Every runtime claim in the rewritten docstring verified true on the patched copy: isinstance(S, Codec) True; isinstance(UInt16, Codec) False (UInt16 has num_bits but no parse/pack); isinstance(UInt16*4, Codec) True; S.pack(s) == s.pack(); parse is a classmethod; a Struct instance also passes the presence-only isinstance and its bound pack() takes no value argument (signature () -> bytes); Array.parse returns a list and pack re-encodes it. The 'num_bits // 8 bytes' phrasing is exact, not approximate: a non-byte-multiple Struct is rejected at class definition (PlanCompileError 'total size is 4 bits, not a whole number of bytes') and sub-byte scalar Arrays are rejected too ('Array of UInt3: sub-byte scalar arrays are not supported'), so every Codec member is byte-aligned by construction. Existing test_codec_protocol assertions (structs_test.py:511-512) unaffected; suite green. No .pyi declares Codec anywhere (checked), so the structs.py Protocol is the sole definition to keep in sync. The optional test in the tests field also checks out (verified (UInt16*2).pack([1,2]) == b'\x00\x01\x00\x02'); note it was NOT counted in the 856 (2 new structs-1 tests + 1 rewritten structs-2 test over an 854 baseline), which is consistent with it being offered as optional. Style matches the file's narrative RST. No issues.
